This was the strongest classic ABIDE pipeline (Abraham 2017; Dadi 2019). Shrinkage keeps the matrices stable for short scans, where the number of ROIs is close to the number of timepoints. I'm replacing Pearson correlation with tangent-space connectivity. The ABIDE benchmarks (Abraham 2017; Dadi 2019) found this to be the strongest classic pipeline. For each subject, I estimate a Ledoit-Wolf shrunk covariance of the standardized CC200 time series. I then whiten it with a group reference (the log-Euclidean mean, computed without labels) and take the matrix log. This projects the covariance matrices onto a flat tangent space, where a linear classifier respects their geometry and between-subject variability is reduced. The classifier is unchanged.

This round makes one change. It replaces the Fisher-z Pearson features with a tangent-space embedding of Ledoit-Wolf shrunk covariances on the same CC200 atlas. Abraham 2017 found this the strongest classic pipeline on ABIDE, because it respects the curved geometry of covariance matrices and whitens each subject relative to the group mean. The scanner and protocol differences between ABIDE sites are large. They shift the connectivity features, so the classifier spends its weak (C=0.001) budget on differences between sites, even though scoring is AUROC within each site. This change removes those site offsets by standardizing each feature within its site before the global scaler and L2 logistic regression. Site statistics come from that site's train and test items together, without labels, and sites with fewer than 4 items fall back to the global statistics.
